To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

IDO expressed by tumor cells promotes tumor growth and immune evasion by recruiting and activating MDSCs through a Treg-dependent mechanism, and that treatment with a selective ID O inhibitor can reverse this immunosuppressive microenvironment.

1) IDO expression by tumor cells results in aggressive tumor growth and immune suppression; 2) Tregs are required for the immunosuppressive effect of IDO; 3) IDO recruits and activates MDSCs in tumors; and 4) IDO inhibitor treatment reduces tumor growth and immune suppressive mechanisms in tumors.

(1) Tumors expressing IDO recruit and activate MDSCs, which are known to suppress T cells; (2) Tregs are required for this recruitment and activation; (3) Tumors with high expression of IDO have more MDSCs; (4) Treatment with a selective inhibitor of IDO decreases MDSCs and their function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of drugs that can be used to treat cancer.
the role of IDO and Tregs in the regulation of tumor-associated immune suppression.
understanding the mechanisms of tumor immune escape and developing new immunotherapies for cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IDO is one of the central mechanisms of immunosuppressive in the tumor micro-environment and targeting of IDO is a promising strategy in immunotherapy.
